source: The Limitation Act, 1908 (Act No. IX of 1908), Laws of Bangladesh

metadata.commencement: Section 1 and section 31 came into force at once; the rest on 1 January 1909
metadata.purpose: Consolidate and amend law for limitation of suits, appeals and applications to Courts; provide rules for acquiring by possession the ownership of easements and other property.
objectives: Promote timely justice: claims filed while evidence and witnesses are fresh
Prevent endless litigation: finality to legal disputes; stale claims barred
Protect defendants from being threatened with suits indefinitely
Encourage diligence in enforcing legal rights
Improve court efficiency: automatic dismissal of late cases under Section 3
amendments: Bangladesh Laws (Revision and Declaration) Act, 1973 (VIII of 1973): terminology substitutions; omitted Arts 1 and 45
Indian Limitation (Amendment) Act, 1929 (I of 1929): inserted Arts 48A, 48B, 134A, 134B, 134C
Repealing and Amending Act, 1937 (XX of 1937): omitted Art 4
Extinction of Discriminatory Privileges Act, 1949 (II of 1950): omitted Art 150A
Civil Procedure and Limitation (Amendment) Ordinance, 1961 (IX of 1961): inserted Art 64A
Limitation (Amendment) Act, 2004 (XXVIII of 2004), w.e.f. 01-07-2005: Arts 113 and 114 reduced to ONE year
Repealing and Amending Act, 1930: repealed sections 30-31 and Second/Third Schedules
Second Repealing and Amending Act, 1914: repealed section 32

definitions.definition: Includes any person from or through whom an applicant derives his right to apply.
Includes a hundi and a cheque.

Includes any instrument whereby a person obliges himself to pay money to another, on condition that the obligation shall be void if a specified act is performed, or is not performed, as the case may be.
Includes any person from or through whom a defendant derives his liability to be sued.

Includes a right not arising from contract, by which one person is entitled to remove and appropriate for his own profit any part of the soil belonging to another, or anything growing in, attached to, or subsisting upon the land of another.
Nothing shall be deemed to be done in good faith which is not done with due care and attention.
Includes any person from or through whom a plaintiff derives his right to sue.
Any instrument whereby the maker engages absolutely to pay a specified sum of money to another at a time therein limited, or on demand, or at sight.
Does NOT include an appeal or application.
Does NOT include a benamidar, a mortgagee remaining in possession after the mortgage has been satisfied, or a wrong-doer in possession without title.

sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement
sections.gist: Act called Limitation Act, 1908; extends to whole of Bangladesh; s.1 & s.31 in force at once, rest from 1 January 1909.

sections.title: Definitions
sections.gist: Defines applicant, bill of exchange, bond, defendant, easement, foreign country, good faith, plaintiff, promissory note, suit, trustee.
key_points: 'good faith' requires due care and attention
'suit' excludes appeals and applications
'trustee' excludes benamidar and satisfied mortgagee in possession

sections.part: II - Limitation of Suits, Appeals, Applications
sections.title: Dismissal of suits instituted after period of limitation
sections.gist: Every suit/appeal/application filed after the First Schedule period SHALL be dismissed, although limitation has not been set up as a defence.
key_points: Subject to provisions of sections 4 to 25
Suit instituted when plaint presented to proper officer; for a pauper when leave application made; for company being wound up when claim sent to official liquidator

sections.title: Where Court is closed when period expires
sections.gist: If limitation expires on a day the Court is closed, the suit/appeal/application may be filed on the day the Court re-opens.

sections.title: Extension of period in certain cases
sections.gist: Appeals, revision/review applications and applications covered by enactment may be admitted after limitation on sufficient cause.
key_points: Applicant must satisfy the Court of sufficient cause
Being misled by an order/practice/judgment of the High Court Division in computing limitation may be sufficient cause
Does NOT extend limitation for instituting a suit

sections.title: Legal disability
sections.gist: If person entitled was minor, insane or idiot when period began, he may sue within the same period AFTER the disability ceases.
key_points: Two disabilities: period runs after both cease
Disability continuing to death: legal representative gets same period after death
Representative under disability: sub-s.(1)/(2) apply

sections.title: Disability of one of several plaintiffs/applicants
sections.gist: If discharge can be given without the disabled co-plaintiff's concurrence, time runs against all; otherwise time does not run against any until one can give discharge or disability ceases.

sections.title: Special exceptions
sections.gist: Sections 6-7 do NOT apply to pre-emption suits; disability extension cannot exceed 3 years from cessation of disability or death.

sections.title: Continuous running of time
sections.gist: Once time begins to run, no subsequent disability or inability to sue stops it.
key_points: Proviso: where debtor obtains letters of administration of creditor's estate, time suspended while administration continues

sections.title: Suits against express trustees and representatives
sections.gist: No suit against express trustee (or representatives/assigns not for value) to follow trust property/proceeds or for account is barred by any length of time.
key_points: Hindu/Muslim/Buddhist religious or charitable endowment property deemed trust property; its manager deemed trustee

sections.title: Suits on foreign contracts
sections.gist: Suits in Bangladesh on foreign contracts governed by THIS Act; foreign limitation a defence only if it extinguished the contract AND parties were domiciled there during that period.

sections.title: Exclusion of time in legal proceedings
sections.gist: The day from which the period is reckoned is EXCLUDED.
key_points: Appeals/leave/review: day judgment pronounced AND time to obtain copy of decree/sentence/order excluded
Appeal from/review of decree: time to obtain copy of judgment also excluded
Application to set aside award: time to obtain copy of award excluded

sections.title: Defendant's absence from Bangladesh
sections.gist: Time during which the defendant was absent from Bangladesh and territories beyond under Government administration is excluded in computing limitation for suits.

sections.title: Bona fide proceeding in Court without jurisdiction
sections.gist: Time prosecuting another civil proceeding with due diligence, in good faith, on the same cause of action, in a Court lacking jurisdiction, is excluded.
key_points: Expl I: both first day and last day of former proceeding counted
Expl II: plaintiff/applicant resisting an appeal is 'prosecuting' a proceeding
Expl III: misjoinder of parties/causes of action deemed a defect like want of jurisdiction

sections.title: Exclusion during suspension
sections.gist: Time of continuance of injunction/order staying institution or execution excluded (issue and withdrawal days both excluded); statutory notice period also excluded.

sections.title: Proceedings to set aside execution-sale pending
sections.gist: For possession suit by purchaser at execution-sale, time during which a proceeding to set aside the sale was prosecuted is excluded.

sections.title: Death before right to sue accrues
sections.gist: If the would-be plaintiff or defendant dies before the right accrues, limitation computed from when a capable legal representative exists.
key_points: Not applicable to pre-emption suits or suits for possession of immovable property or hereditary office

sections.title: Effect of fraud
sections.gist: Where fraud kept the plaintiff from knowledge of the right/title, or a necessary document was fraudulently concealed, time runs from when the fraud first became known (or when he first had means to produce the concealed document).

sections.title: Acknowledgement in writing
sections.gist: Written acknowledgement of liability signed by the liable party (or title-deriver) before expiry of the period starts a FRESH period from signing.
key_points: Undated writing: oral evidence of signing date allowed, not of contents
Sufficient even if it omits exact nature of right, avers time not yet come, includes refusal, set-off claim, or is addressed to another person
'Signed' includes duly authorised agent; execution application is an application in respect of a right

sections.title: Payment on account of debt or interest on legacy
sections.gist: Part payment of debt/interest before expiry by the liable person or authorised agent starts a fresh period from payment.
key_points: Proviso: acknowledgement of payment in payer's handwriting or signed writing required (except interest payments before 1-1-1928)
Mortgagee in possession: receipt of rent/produce deemed payment
'Debt' includes money payable under a decree or order of Court

sections.title: Agent of persons under disability; joint contractors
sections.gist: For persons under disability 'duly authorised agent' includes lawful guardian/committee/manager or their agent.
key_points: One joint contractor/partner/executor/mortgagee's acknowledgement or payment does NOT charge the others
Hindu widow/limited owner's acknowledgement valid against reversioner
HUF manager's acknowledgement/payment deemed made for whole family

sections.title: Substituting or adding new plaintiff/defendant
sections.gist: Suit deemed instituted against/for a newly added party when he was made a party; does not apply to assignment/devolution during pendency or plaintiff-defendant swap.

sections.title: Continuing breaches and wrongs
sections.gist: In continuing breach of contract or continuing wrong, a fresh period of limitation begins to run at every moment during which the breach/wrong continues.

sections.title: Act not actionable without special damage
sections.gist: For compensation where a specific injury must result, limitation runs from the time the injury results.

sections.title: Time mentioned in instruments
sections.gist: All instruments deemed made with reference to the Gregorian calendar.

sections.title: Acquisition of right to easements
sections.gist: 20 years' peaceable, open, as-of-right, uninterrupted enjoyment of light/air/way/watercourse/easement makes the right absolute and indefeasible.
key_points: The 20-year period must end within 2 years before the suit
Against Government property: 60 years substituted for 20
Interruption only where actual discontinuance caused by another's obstruction, submitted/acquiesced in for 1 year after notice
Asking leave once during the period defeats the claim

sections.title: Exclusion in favour of reversioner of servient tenement
sections.gist: Enjoyment during a life interest or term over 3 years is excluded from the 20 years if, within 3 years after it ends, the reversioner resists the claim.

sections.title: Extinguishment of right to property
sections.gist: When the limitation period for a suit for possession of property ends, the person's RIGHT TO THE PROPERTY IS EXTINGUISHED.

sections.title: Savings
sections.gist: Nothing affects s.25 Contract Act 1872; special laws with different periods override the Schedule.
key_points: For special-law periods: s.3 applies; ss.4, 9-18, 22 apply unless expressly excluded; remaining provisions do not apply
Act does NOT apply to suits under the Divorce Act
ss.26-27 and 'easement' definition do not apply where the Easements Act, 1882 extends

sections.title: Repealed
sections.gist: Repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1930 (VIII of 1930).

sections.title: Repealed
sections.gist: Repealed by the Second Repealing and Amending Act, 1914 (XVII of 1914).

cheat_sheet: 10 days: Leave to defend summary suit (Art 159)
15-20 days: Small Cause review (161), restore review (160), HCD original appeal (151), HCD original review (162)
30 days: Most execution/interim applications (163-170), appeal to District Judge (152), CrPC other courts (154), set aside award (158)
60 days: CrPC appeal to HCD (155), set aside abatement (171), insolvent assignee application (172)
90 days: Civil appeal to HCD (156), other reviews (173), legal representative applications (176-177), arbitration award filing (178), leave to appeal to Appellate Division (179)
6 months: Appeal from acquittal (157), decree instalments (175), SRA s.9 possession (Art 3)
1 year: Injury/defamation/penalty/wages/pre-emption torts (Arts 5-31); specific performance (113) and rescission (114) as amended 2004
3 years: Money claims, contracts (unregistered), movable property, negotiable instruments, dower, rent arrears, indemnity, surety (Arts 37-115)
6 years: Breach of registered written contract (116), foreign judgment (117), RESIDUARY suits (120)
12 years: Possession of immovable property (142-144), judgments/recognisances (122), legacies (123), hereditary office (124), enforcement of HCD/AD orders (183)
30 years: Deposits and pawns (145), HCD mortgagee possession (146), local authority streets (146A)
60 years: Mortgagee foreclosure/sale (147), redemption (148), Government suits (149)

faq.q: What is the purpose of the Limitation Act, 1908?
faq.a: To set strict time limits for filing civil suits, appeals and applications, and to provide rules for acquiring ownership by long-term possession. It promotes timely justice (fresh evidence), prevents endless litigation and stale claims, protects defendants from indefinite threat of suits, encourages diligence, and improves court efficiency - late cases are dismissed automatically under Section 3.

faq.q: Is limitation a defence that must be pleaded by the defendant?
faq.a: No. Under Section 3 every suit, appeal or application filed after the prescribed period SHALL be dismissed although limitation has not been set up as a defence - the Court acts on its own.

faq.q: What if the last day of limitation falls on a court holiday?
faq.a: Section 4: the suit, appeal or application may be instituted, preferred or made on the day the Court re-opens.

faq.q: Can an appeal or application be filed late?
faq.a: Yes, under Section 5 only, if the appellant/applicant satisfies the Court of sufficient cause. Being misled by an order, practice or judgment of the High Court Division in computing limitation may be sufficient cause. Note: Section 5 does not extend the period for instituting a suit.

faq.q: What if the plaintiff was a minor or insane when the right to sue accrued?
faq.a: Section 6: the same period runs after the disability (minority/insanity/idiotcy) ceases. If two disabilities exist, time runs after both cease; if disability continues till death, the legal representative gets the same period after death. Section 8 caps extensions at 3 years from cessation and excludes pre-emption suits.

faq.q: How is limitation computed for an appeal?
faq.a: Section 12: the day the judgment was pronounced and the time requisite for obtaining a certified copy of the decree, sentence or order are excluded; for decrees, time to obtain the judgment copy is also excluded. The first day of any period is excluded.

faq.q: What is the period for a suit to recover money lent?
faq.a: Three years under Arts 57-59: from when the loan is made (Art 57/59) or when a cheque given by the lender is paid (Art 58). Demand loans (Art 59) also run from the date of the loan.

faq.q: What is the period to recover possession of immovable property?
faq.a: 12 years: Art 142 (dispossession/discontinuance), Art 144 (residuary - when defendant's possession becomes adverse), Art 139 (landlord vs tenant, when tenancy determined).

faq.q: What is the residuary period if no article fits?
faq.a: Suits: 6 years from when the right to sue accrues (Art 120). Applications: 3 years from when the right to apply accrues (Art 181).

faq.q: How long to execute a civil court decree?
faq.a: Art 182: 3 years (or 6 years where a certified copy of the decree/order has been registered), counted from the decree, the final appellate/review/amended decree, a prior execution step, or the due date of the payment enforced. Judgments of the High Court Division (original civil jurisdiction) and Appellate Division orders: 12 years (Art 183), with fresh computation on revival, payment or written acknowledgement.

faq.q: What is the limitation for a civil appeal to the High Court Division?
faq.a: 90 days (Art 156); to the District Judge 30 days (Art 152); from an HCD original-jurisdiction decree 20 days (Art 151). Criminal: 60 days to HCD (Art 155), 30 days to other courts (Art 154), 7 days against death sentence (Art 150), 6 months against acquittal (Art 157).

faq.q: What is the effect of a written acknowledgement of a debt?
faq.a: Section 19: an acknowledgement of liability in writing signed by the liable party (or one through whom he derives title) made before the period expires starts a FRESH period of limitation from the date of signing.

faq.q: Does part payment of a debt extend limitation?
faq.a: Yes, Section 20: a payment on account of the debt/interest before expiry by the liable person or authorised agent starts a fresh period from the payment - provided the payment is acknowledged in the payer's handwriting or a signed writing (interest payments before 1-1-1928 excepted). A mortgagee's receipt of rent or produce counts as payment.

faq.q: What if fraud concealed my cause of action?
faq.a: Section 18: time runs from when the fraud first became known to the injured person, or (concealed document) from when he first had the means to produce it or compel its production.

faq.q: What about a continuing breach of contract?
faq.a: Section 23: a fresh period of limitation begins at every moment during which the continuing breach or wrong continues.

faq.q: How can an easement be acquired by possession?
faq.a: Section 26: 20 years' peaceable, open, as-of-right, uninterrupted enjoyment makes the right absolute and indefeasible (period must end within 2 years before the suit). Against Government property: 60 years. Asking leave once during the period defeats the claim.

faq.q: Does limitation merely bar the remedy, or extinguish the right?
faq.a: For property: Section 28 - on expiry of the period for a possession suit, the right to the property itself is EXTINGUISHED. Exception: suits against express trustees for trust property (Section 10) are never barred.

faq.q: What is the limitation for a Muslim wife's dower suit?
faq.a: Exigible dower (mu'ajjal): 3 years from demand-and-refusal, or from dissolution of marriage if no demand was made (Art 103). Deferred dower (mu'wajjal): 3 years from dissolution by death or divorce (Art 104).

faq.q: What is the period for arrears of rent?
faq.a: 3 years from when the arrears become due (Art 110).

faq.q: What is the period for specific performance of a contract?
faq.a: One year (Art 113) - changed from 3 years by the Limitation (Amendment) Act, 2004, effective 01-07-2005. Runs from the date fixed for performance or notice of refusal. Rescission of contract is also 1 year (Art 114).

faq.q: Do suits by or against the Government have special limitation?
faq.a: Suits by or on behalf of the Government: 60 years (Art 149), computed as for a private person. Suits against Government (e.g., revenue matters, land acquisition compensation): generally 1 year (Arts 15-18).

faq.q: What is the period for compensation for personal injury, libel or slander?
faq.a: Injury to the person: 1 year from when the injury is committed (Art 22). Libel: 1 year from publication (Art 24). Slander: 1 year from the words spoken, or where not actionable in themselves, from when the special damage results (Art 25).

faq.q: Trespass on land - which article applies?
faq.a: Compensation for trespass: 3 years from the trespass (Art 39). A suit to RECOVER POSSESSION: 12 years (Arts 142/144).
